name: Goose
tagline: An extensible AI agent with a Rust core, command-line interface, and Electron desktop app.
hook: A Rust desktop guide to issue readiness, parallel agent loops, retiring MCP code, and a macOS executable-replacement trap.
summary: Goose checks whether an issue is ready before implementation and records constraints from its Rust desktop app. The guide covers old and new agent loops running side by side, a retiring MCP directory, and a macOS failure caused by overwriting a running executable.

techniques.title: Require an agreed plan before implementing external work
techniques.body: The contribution workflow requires a Ready issue with design, constraints, non-goals, and verification already recorded. A material design change sends implementation back to the issue discussion.
techniques.quote: - If implementation reveals a material design change, return to the issue before continuing.

techniques.title: Maintain behavioral parity during a migration
techniques.body: The guide identifies the legacy loop and the state-machine replacement. Until migration is complete, an agent must implement and test applicable behavior in both paths.
techniques.quote: Until the migration is complete, changes to agent-loop behavior must be implemented and tested in both paths.

techniques.title: Freeze additions without blocking migration maintenance
techniques.body: New third-party entries in the old MCP directory are no longer accepted, while changes that maintain or remove entries remain possible. The policy makes the migration direction explicit without treating legacy data as untouchable.
techniques.quote: - Treat the existing goose directory as legacy data while registry-backed discovery and installation are implemented.

techniques.title: Attach an operating-system failure to a file-operation rule
techniques.body: The Never section forbids overwriting a live executable and names unlinking or atomic rename as alternatives. It explains that macOS can kill running processes because the code signature becomes invalid.
techniques.quote: - Never: Overwrite a live binary in place (e.g. `cp`/`fs.copyFileSync` onto an existing executable) - unlink or atomic-rename the destination first, otherwise macOS SIGKILLs running processes with "Code Signature Invalid"

steal: Require design agreement before externally contributed implementation.
Document parity obligations while old and new systems coexist.
Separate prohibited legacy expansion from allowed migration work.
Pair unsafe file operations with their concrete failure modes and alternatives.
